entry.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 3.7 Flash, an improved AI model for coding and agents with better accuracy and lower cost [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini 3.7 Flash, an upgraded AI model designed to enhance coding, knowledge work, and web development workflows. This model offers improved debugging, higher code accuracy, and better performance in generating production-ready code, while reducing costs to half of its predecessor, Gemini 3.6 Flash. Gemini 3.7 Flash also improves developer experience by adapting better to challenges and following instructions more precisely, enabling more efficient multi-step planning and tool use. It is integrated into Gemini Spark, Google's personal AI agent, to enhance productivity in Google Workspace apps. The model includes updated safety safeguards against misuse in sensitive domains and is available to developers, enterprises, and individuals through various Google platforms.

entry.title: Cerebras and OpenAI launch Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, delivering up to 750 tokens per second with no quality loss, initially for select customers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Cerebras and OpenAI have introduced Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, a new service tier in the OpenAI API that accelerates output speeds up to 750 tokens per second without compromising quality. This mode is initially available to select customers and aims to support time-sensitive, mission-critical applications by resolving the traditional tradeoff between speed and intelligence in AI models. Benchmark tests show GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast answered 2,500 challenging questions in just over 11 hours, nearly seven times faster than comparable models, while maintaining accuracy. Powered by Cerebras' Wafer-Scale Engine architecture, Ultrafast mode reduces data movement bottlenecks common in GPU inference, enabling faster responses for applications such as legal briefs, financial models, and engineering reports. Ultrafast mode is designed to enhance workflows where rapid AI inference is critical, including real-time incident response and cybersecurity. It allows organizations to deploy AI agents that keep pace with human thinking and collaboration, potentially transforming productivity and enabling new modes of working with AI.

entry.title: Mistral releases OCR 4.1 with paragraph-level bounding box extraction and block-level confidence scores for document AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Mistral has launched OCR 4.1, an updated optical character recognition service designed to enhance its Document AI capabilities. The new version includes native paragraph-level bounding box extraction, structural block labels, and block-level confidence scores to improve document processing accuracy. This release is part of Mistral's broader AI model offerings, which also include Z.ai GLM 5.2, Shieldstral 1.0, and Mistral Medium 3.5, indicating ongoing development in their AI technology stack.

entry.title: Developer builds a home AI system using repurposed server GPUs and salvaged PC parts amid hardware shortages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A software developer describes assembling a personal AI computing setup at home using overproduced AMD server GPUs originally intended for cloud gaming, combined with salvaged PC components due to current hardware shortages. The project aims to create a local AI data center to avoid reliance on external cloud services and maintain control over the technology. The build includes four AMD V620 GPUs with 32GB VRAM each, an Intel Core i9 10900X CPU, and a motherboard with four PCIe x16 slots, all sourced from used or surplus hardware markets. Custom cooling solutions were designed and 3D-printed to address the lack of built-in fans on the server GPUs, enabling efficient airflow for the stacked cards. This approach reflects a practical and cost-conscious method to enable AI workloads at home despite the high cost and scarcity of new AI-optimized hardware.

entry.title: Researchers introduce MBA-Bench, a multimodal benchmark and agents for business ideation using visual and textual data across six domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed MBA-Bench, the first multimodal benchmark designed to train and evaluate business ideation agents using both visual and textual inputs. The benchmark includes 30,000 samples across six domains, each with unique visual cues that text alone cannot fully capture, and uses GPT-4o to generate reference ideas for business questions. Two agent models, MBA-b and MBA-k, are trained with novel reward objectives focusing on creativity and feasibility, outperforming baseline models by significant margins in extensive experiments. MBA-Bench evaluates agents on six business-oriented criteria using a multimodal large language model as a judge, with MBA-b handling blind criteria settings and MBA-k optimizing known criteria. Training involves LoRA-based supervised fine-tuning followed by group relative policy optimization. The multimodal agents approach the performance of closed-source models on several metrics, demonstrating the value of integrating visual information for real-world business ideation tasks.

entry.title: Researchers propose REOPD, a reliability-adaptive reward extrapolation method for on-policy distillation that improves training stability and performance across multiple domains without extra models or rollouts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: REOPD is a new framework for on-policy distillation that adjusts reward extrapolation at the token level using a compatibility weight combined with a batch-level adaptive budget. This approach preserves alignment with the teacher model while selectively amplifying reliable signals, avoiding reward hacking and unstable training caused by global coefficients. The method requires no additional verifier, reward model, value model, or rollouts beyond standard on-policy distillation. In experiments, REOPD outperforms previous methods like G-OPD on single-teacher mathematics tasks and multi-teacher settings, while matching performance on single-teacher code tasks. This demonstrates its ability to adapt reward extrapolation finely across different domains and teacher configurations, reducing the need for costly hyperparameter tuning.

entry.title: Researchers identify Information Abundance Paradox where longer training contexts reduce parametric knowledge in large language models, impacting performance and robustness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers propose the Information Abundance Paradox, showing that training large language models with longer context windows can decrease the models' parametric knowledge by increasing reliance on context. Their study finds that while longer contexts initially improve language modeling and understanding, performance declines beyond an optimal context length, and fine-tuning with more context reduces robustness when context is missing or misleading at test time. The shift in learning dynamics moves gradient pressure from feed-forward networks to attention modules, suggesting that simply scaling context length is not a straightforward path to better model knowledge retention or inference.

entry.title: Researchers propose operational definitions framing AI reasoning as a learnable rule-based process to address ambiguity in autonomous reasoning evaluation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A new paper on arXiv argues that the lack of clear operational definitions for reasoning in generative AI hampers the ability to evaluate and advance trustworthy autonomous reasoning. The authors propose definitions that position valid and sound reasoning as a learnable rule-based process and provide a checklist to improve communication in AI reasoning research. This approach aims to resolve definitional ambiguity and enable measurable progress toward reliable autonomous reasoning systems.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Causal Attribution Score (CAS) for local and global causal explanations in AI, outperforming traditional methods in benchmarks and empirical datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed the Causal Attribution Score (CAS), a method that provides causal explanations for AI model outputs by attributing intervention effects on real-world outcomes. CAS uses an interventional coalition game framework with causal Shapley contributions to generate local and global causal explanations, distinguishing causal effect heterogeneity from mere outcome prediction. Benchmark tests with simulated data showed CAS achieves lower mean absolute error compared to traditional normalization methods, especially under strong interactions. Empirical analyses on datasets involving 401(k) eligibility and unemployment benefits revealed that CAS rankings of treatment-effect modifiers differ significantly from predictive SHAP rankings, highlighting the importance of separating causal explanations from predictive importance in AI models.

entry.title: Researchers introduce DiG-bench, a 70-game benchmark to test AI discovery of unknown rules and objectives through experimentation, with seven difficulty levels and partial public release [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed DiG-bench, a new benchmark consisting of 70 independent games designed to evaluate AI systems' ability to discover novel knowledge by interacting with unknown game rules and win conditions. The benchmark includes seven tiers of difficulty, ranging from levels solvable by current models to challenges for advanced AI agents, with 21 games publicly available and the rest held private for secure evaluation. Each game has been solved by at least one human on the first attempt, demonstrating human capability in these discovery tasks.

entry.title: Researchers introduce a system to measure and repair constraint adherence failures in multi-turn dialogues with black-box large language models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A recent study presents a system that addresses "behavioral relapse" in multi-turn dialogues with large language models (LLMs), where models continue to follow revoked constraints. The system uses a contract ledger to track constraints and revocations, measures adherence per clause, and applies repairs within resource limits, making revocation failure measurable and manageable. Experiments show that stronger models exhibit less relapse, and the proposed methods significantly reduce constraint violations compared to baseline approaches. The system can predict relapse before response delivery and partially recover from it with simple interventions, improving dialogue state management in LLM interactions.

entry.title: Researchers introduce SteerBench-Work, a benchmark for evaluating AI agent decisions to proceed or hold actions across workplace domains using 106 incident-based scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: SteerBench-Work is a new benchmark designed to assess how long-running large language model (LLM) agents decide whether to proceed with or hold actions at critical boundaries in workplace settings such as developer operations, customer service, finance, legal, medical, HR, and security. The benchmark includes 106 scenarios based on public incidents, with balanced labels for proceed and hold decisions, allowing models to be scored on their accuracy in crossing or holding action boundaries correctly. Testing across 30 model conditions revealed that models tend to err by over-holding authorized actions 28.1% of the time, while allowing unsafe actions only 1.0% of the time. The most challenging cases involve risk-resolved commits where evidence has cleared risks, and models perform worse on evidence-reversed mirror scenarios compared to original incidents. The study highlights that general AI capability does not equate to proper steering calibration, as higher-capability models often over-refuse actions, and additional reasoning can improve weak gates without affecting well-calibrated ones. A public leaderboard for SteerBench-Work is available at steerbench.com.

entry.title: Researchers design AI pipeline transforming ITSM ticket data into decision-support artifacts with high stakeholder trust and actionability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A new sociotechnical AI pipeline has been developed to convert large volumes of heterogeneous IT service management (ITSM) ticket data into multilevel decision-support artifacts for sales and executive stakeholders. The pipeline integrates LLM-based schema normalization, HDBSCAN sub-topic clustering, and hierarchical agglomerative clustering to produce executive-facing main topics and detailed sub-topics, aiming to improve interpretability and actionability of ITSM analytics. The pipeline was evaluated by five raters from Sales Engineering and customer success roles across six artifacts, scoring above 4.0 out of 5.0 on metrics including interpretability, actionability, trust, and likelihood of use, with trust being the most consistent. The study frames ITSM analytics as an Information Systems challenge involving transformation, abstraction, and human-centered design principles.

entry.title: Researchers introduce DECAF to decompose perturbation responses into evidence, contradiction, and fragility, improving interpretation of model decisions across vision and tabular tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers present DECAF (Decomposition of Evidence, Contradiction, And Fragility), a method that breaks down perturbation response magnitudes into components reflecting aligned evidence, opposing contradiction, and endpoint-null fragility to better interpret model decision changes under input alterations. This decomposition preserves total response magnitude and is unique under endpoint-relative axioms, enabling more nuanced analysis than magnitude alone. In experiments across controlled vision and tabular datasets, including a 72-model ImageNet-9 audit, DECAF components correlated strongly with independently measured behaviors, with the largest component matching observed behavior in 96.4% of cases compared to 35.0% for magnitude alone. The method also demonstrated efficiency gains on large-scale models like a 1B-parameter DINOv2, achieving comparable attribution quality to gradient-based baselines with significantly lower computation time and memory usage.

entry.title: Researchers propose Global-Impact Cache (GCache) to optimize cache reuse policies in diffusion models, achieving 2.17x speedup and improved visual quality on Wan2.1 video diffusion [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers introduce Global-Impact Cache (GCache), a new cache reuse policy for diffusion models that addresses misalignment between local similarity heuristics and final generation quality by modeling error propagation along the denoising trajectory. GCache uses a bilevel optimization framework to identify optimal reuse policies that prioritize computation impacting visual fidelity, balancing theoretical rigor with empirical performance. Extensive experiments show GCache outperforms prior caching strategies in both video and image generation tasks. On the state-of-the-art Wan2.1 video diffusion model, GCache achieves a 2.17x inference speedup while significantly reducing perceptual error, lowering LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316, demonstrating improved generation quality alongside efficiency gains.

entry.title: Researchers develop VALG, an autonomous agentic system for machine learning theory research that adaptively formulates problems and manages graph-structured proofs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: VALG is designed to automate the process of formulating hypotheses, testing them, and refining proofs in machine learning theory by maintaining mathematical specifications and verifying proof dependencies. The system identifies obstructions in proofs and adapts by generating related variants or relaxations while preserving mathematical relations to the original problems. Evaluated on nine subproblems from five COLT 2026 open problems, VALG produced finalized theorem candidates matching source scopes and yielded conditional or restricted results in other cases, demonstrating its ability to keep different proof outcomes mathematically distinct. VALG is available as open source software.

entry.title: Researchers analyze explanatory engagement of open-weight LLMs under varying rare failure rates, finding engagement patterns depend on elicitation conditions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers studied how three open-weight large language models (qwen3:8b, llama3.1:8b, mistral:7b) adjust their explanatory engagement-measured by explanation length, specificity, and confidence-when exposed to tool-call failures at probabilities ranging from 0.2 to 0.0001. They tested five elicitation conditions, from immediate prompting to none, to observe whether engagement rises as failures become rarer and then collapses near detectability thresholds. Results showed that overall explanation length decreased monotonically, but when analyzed by condition, immediate forced explanations confirmed a rise in engagement followed by a plateau, while other conditions showed different patterns including unprompted self-monitoring in llama3.1:8b. A companion guaranteed-failure experiment revealed model differences in anomaly recognition separate from engagement. The study highlights elicitation structure as a key factor in observing engagement changes and notes limitations due to discrete failure rates tested.

entry.title: Researchers test capability sheaves for compositional agent-harness repair using controlled quotients and real-repository data from 20 repositories and 160 issues [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers propose modeling failures in agent harnesses, which combine retrieval, routing, state, provenance, and verification, using finite capability sheaves that encode behavior signatures and shared state. They formulate acceptance as a constraint-satisfaction problem and introduce a cohomology-based diagnostic to reduce candidate repair budgets in controlled experiments over 20 task clusters. The method was evaluated on a real-world dataset from the SWE-bench Multilingual pool, involving 160 issues across 20 repositories with 875 candidate patches. Results showed that the cohomological approach matched but did not significantly outperform noncohomological selectors in resolving issues, and a discovery gate failed to generalize across repositories. The study supports the invariance mechanism and identifiability correction but finds no clear advantage for cohomological methods in practical repair tasks.

entry.title: Study compares six multilingual pretrained models for Nepali ASR, finding language-family proximity can offset scale and CTC decoders offer faster inference [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers conducted a controlled benchmark comparing six multilingual pretrained models for Nepali automatic speech recognition (ASR) using the OpenSLR SLR54 corpus with consistent fine-tuning protocols. They evaluated models including XLSR-53, IndicWav2Vec, MMS-1B, Whisper variants, and Conformer-Hi across three test sets, measuring word error rate (WER), character error rate (CER), and real-time factor (RTF). Whisper-Large-v3-Turbo and IndicWav2Vec achieved the best accuracy despite large differences in model size and pretraining data, suggesting that language-family proximity in pretraining can substitute for scale in Nepali ASR.

entry.title: Study finds suppressing carbon price signals in Italy's power market reduces short-term costs but increases CO2 emissions and undermines renewable investment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers analyzed Italy's 2026 Decreto Bollette policy, which proposes removing carbon price equivalents from certain gas power plant bids, using a multi-agent reinforcement learning model to assess long-term effects on investment, emissions, and consumer costs. The study found that while partial suppression of carbon pricing lowers short-term electricity costs, it leads to higher CO2 emissions and reduced incentives for renewable and storage investments over time. Only scenarios with strong support for green investments avoided increased emissions, but these required sidelining the wholesale price signal, conflicting with the policy's original intent.

entry.title: Researchers propose GraphGym, a semi-automatic multi-dimensional benchmark for complex graph reasoning in large language models with 202 tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed GraphGym, a semi-automatic framework to create a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating large language models' graph reasoning abilities across five dimensions including graph size and task complexity. The benchmark includes 202 tasks and supports text-based, code-based, and augmented reasoning evaluations, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks that rely on manual construction and lack unified evaluation modes. GraphGym uses an LLM-based data generator to produce task descriptions, graph data, reference solutions, and evaluation scripts, with human validation at key stages to ensure quality. Experiments reveal that current fine-tuned models struggle to generalize on this benchmark, while retrieval-augmented methods improve textual reasoning but not consistently coding reasoning, highlighting areas for future model enhancement. The code and dataset will be released soon.

entry.title: Researchers present X-AddGraph, a post-hoc explainability framework for AddGraph's recurrent graph anomaly detection, preserving detection accuracy while providing spatial-temporal attributions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed X-AddGraph, a post-hoc explainability framework for AddGraph, a GCN+GRU-based model for edge-level anomaly detection in dynamic graphs. X-AddGraph introduces a Dual Spatial-Temporal Attribution mechanism aligned with AddGraph's architecture, offering gradient-based spatial relevance, contextual attention weights for short-term temporal attribution, and gradient rollback for long-term temporal attribution, all without affecting detection performance. On the UCI Message benchmark, the AddGraph baseline achieved an average per-snapshot AUC of 0.8705, surpassing previous results, while X-AddGraph reproduced these scores exactly and added explanations where none existed. The long-term attribution component identified historical snapshots with significantly more counterfactual signal than random selection, a capability not available in spatially-blind explainers. The researchers have released their implementation to support reproducibility.

entry.title: Researchers propose SSPO, a structure-aware similarity-weighted preference optimization method for neural combinatorial optimization, showing improved performance on TSP, EFL, and JSP benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers introduce SSPO (Structure-Aware Similarity-Weighted Preference Optimization), a method that jointly scores sampled solutions using a dissimilarity-weighted leave-one-out baseline to address limitations in existing neural combinatorial optimization training approaches. SSPO leverages problem-adaptive solution embeddings derived from encoder node representations to weight structurally distinct solutions higher, reducing gradient variance and improving training signals. Experiments demonstrate consistent performance gains over prior best-anchor and uniform-weight baselines on Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP), Electric Facility Location (EFL), and Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSP) benchmarks. The SSPO-trained EFL policy has been deployed in a production facility-location system at JD.com, confirming its practical viability at scale.

entry.title: Researchers propose a learning-based hypnogram model that aggregates multiple expert labels to improve sleep stage classification accuracy on public EEG and EMG datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: This study addresses variability in sleep stage classification by developing a learning-based hypnogram (LBH) that models individual scorer behavior using confusion matrices from machine learning classifiers. The approach aggregates probabilities from multiple experts to assign more reliable sleep stage labels, evaluated on the DOD-H and DOD-O datasets using EEG and chin EMG signals segmented into 30-second epochs. LBH outperformed traditional single-scorer references, achieving over 86% accuracy and 85% precision with random forest classifiers using combined EEG and EMG features. These results suggest that personalized scorer modeling can enhance the construction of reference hypnograms without discarding individual expert information.

entry.title: Researchers propose valuation-anchored similarity metric using CatBoost to identify peer companies in private markets, improving valuation tasks across 270,000 firms globally [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers propose a supervised similarity learning framework that defines company similarity based on market valuation rather than static features or semantic descriptions, addressing challenges in private markets such as limited transparency and sparse data. They train a CatBoost gradient-boosted decision tree model on observed private company valuations and derive a valuation-aware similarity metric from importance-weighted leaf-node co-occurrences, capturing shared valuation drivers while handling nonlinear relationships and missing data. Using a dataset of approximately 270,000 private companies worldwide, including over 53,000 with observed or derivable post-money valuations across various industries, geographies, and deal stages, the study demonstrates that this valuation-anchored similarity metric outperforms traditional distance-based and text-embedding approaches in k-nearest-neighbor valuation tasks, while maintaining case-based explainability.

entry.title: Researchers develop orientation-resolved formula to predict latent dimension size for training neural networks with random low-dimensional reparameterizations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers propose a theoretical framework to predict how large a latent search space must be for neural networks trained via random low-dimensional reparameterization to reach low-loss regions. They introduce an orientation-resolved quadratic master formula that accounts for curvature and displacement profiles, improving predictions over previous bounds. The team also presents Random Mapping Networks (RaMaN), which use structured random maps to reduce memory requirements during training. Experiments demonstrate that their predictor closely matches observed training transitions in image and language models, outperforming orientation-agnostic methods when displacement direction is significant.

entry.title: Researchers propose Bayesian method for interpretable causal discovery using causal-effect constraints and rare-event estimation techniques [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers present a Bayesian inference approach to conditional causal discovery that targets the posterior over causal graphs and parameters given causal-effect constraints. Their method addresses computational challenges in existing Bayesian causal discovery techniques by adapting rare-event estimation to sample the joint graph-parameter space, enabling interpretation and explanation of causal phenomena such as large causal effects. The approach gradually guides a particle population toward constrained regions while maintaining samples approximating the conditional posterior. Empirical evaluations on synthetic graphs demonstrate accuracy at various scales, and a case study on the Sachs protein dataset illustrates how the method can support scientific exploration by providing pathway-level summaries.

entry.title: Researchers introduce scalable restricted logit modeling to estimate demand transfer coefficients for assortments exceeding one million items, improving demand forecasting accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers present a method to estimate Demand Transfer (DT) coefficients that quantify how demand shifts among items when a target item is removed from a store's assortment. This approach combines independent item demand forecasts with adjustments accounting for substitution effects, enabling efficient demand forecasting across large item universes with over one million products. Experiments using historical transaction data across multiple locations and categories demonstrate that the method accurately estimates DT coefficients under reasonable substitution assumptions and enhances demand prediction performance.

entry.title: Researchers propose Step-Level Self-Distilled Policy Optimization to improve deep search agents by using evidence anchors and step-level advantage weights, outperforming prior methods on Qwen3-8B [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers introduce Step-Level Self-Distilled Policy Optimization (SSPO) to enhance deep search agents that operate over long trajectories, addressing the challenge of sparse outcome rewards in reinforcement learning. SSPO uses concise evidence snippets called Evidence Anchors as privileged information and converts teacher-student disagreements into step-level advantage weights, applied only to incorrect trajectories to improve learning without compromising diversity. The method decouples the direction and magnitude of policy updates, with outcome rewards guiding direction and the teacher modulating update size at each step. Evaluated on the Qwen3-8B model across BrowseComp, GAIA, and FRAMES benchmarks, SSPO consistently outperforms or matches the performance of GRPO trained with twice as many gradient steps, adding only about 5% computational overhead per step from an additional forward pass.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Tree-Coupled A/B Testing for exact multi-policy comparison with reduced reward queries and improved cost-precision trade-offs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers propose Tree-Coupled A/B Testing (TCAB), a method for comparing multiple adaptive decision policies that shares feedback across policies to reduce the number of reward queries needed. TCAB connects policy histories via a tree structure, allowing policies to retain their individual trajectory laws while sharing rewards, resulting in a query count close to the single-policy baseline rather than scaling linearly with the number of policies. The approach is conditionally optimal among edge-local designs and uses a minimum-spanning tree to minimize costs. Theoretical results show sublinear pseudo-regret and finite-sample variance bounds for pairwise policy contrasts. Experiments on reward-model evaluation, language-model multiple-choice evaluation, and adaptive search policies demonstrate significant improvements in efficiency and precision compared to independent A/B/n testing.

entry.title: Researchers propose FSGR framework to mitigate token frequency bias in SID-based generative recommendation, improving fairness by over 20% while maintaining accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Semantic ID (SID)-based generative recommendation systems face a fairness issue called token frequency bias, where high-frequency tokens are over-predicted and low-frequency tokens under-predicted, leading to unfair item exposure. Researchers introduce FSGR, a fairness optimization framework that balances SID representation and applies hierarchical frequency calibration during training to address this bias. FSGR uses optimal transport-based assignment optimization and a dual-criteria re-anchor mechanism during SID construction to create a balanced token space. It also employs a two-stage training strategy with layer-specific fairness fine-tuning. Experiments on three public datasets with multiple backbone models show that FSGR reduces token frequency bias and improves Gini fairness metrics by over 20% without sacrificing recommendation accuracy.

entry.title: Researchers develop a compositional theory of curvature in probabilistic circuits, introducing an adaptive sharpness-aware regularizer to improve generalization and preserve EM updates [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers propose a compositional theory of curvature for probabilistic circuits (PCs), generative models that allow exact inference and tractable curvature measurement via the Hessian trace of the log-likelihood. They demonstrate that global sharpness regularization can be misspecified for PCs due to their inherently compositional curvature, and prove that each sum node's contribution to curvature factorizes into circuit flow and a local sharpness term. Building on this, they introduce an adaptive sharpness-aware regularizer that penalizes nodes based on local curvature while preserving closed-form expectation-maximization updates. Empirical results show this targeted regularization recovers generalization performance lost by global regularization, maintaining robustness and benefits of sharpness-aware learning.

entry.title: Researchers propose EGRL, a graph neural network framework with edge generation and relation-aware learning to improve RNA-protein interaction prediction, especially for unknown molecules [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Edge Generation-guided Relation-aware Learning (EGRL), a novel deep learning framework designed to predict RNA-protein interactions (RPIs) more effectively. EGRL addresses limitations of existing graph neural network methods by learning implicit meta-paths, using multi-relation-aware attention, generating potential edges to support cold-start nodes, and fusing multiple features for interaction scoring. It is trained jointly with primary and auxiliary losses to enhance performance. Evaluations on four benchmark datasets show that EGRL achieves competitive overall results and significantly improves generalization in cold-start scenarios involving unknown molecules. It attained an AUROC of 0.867 and an AUPR of 0.861 on unknown molecules, representing improvements of 8.6% and 5.0% respectively over prior state-of-the-art methods. The researchers plan to release the code soon.

entry.title: Researchers adapt Expected Threat and VAEP frameworks to handball using five seasons of Bundesliga data, introducing H-xT and H-VAEP models with improved player action valuation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed the first comprehensive adaptation of Expected Threat (xT) and Valuing Actions by Estimating Probabilities (VAEP) frameworks for professional handball, using tracking data from five seasons of the Handball Bundesliga. They introduced Handball-xT (H-xT) with a handball-specific court zoning layout and optimized Handball-VAEP (H-VAEP) by customizing features and context length to reduce team-identity bias, resulting in stable and intuitive player ratings that emphasize build-up play. The study demonstrates that H-xT is more robust than traditional rectangular grid methods through simulations, and H-VAEP provides discriminative player evaluations. The researchers have also released their full code repository to facilitate adoption by professional clubs seeking advanced player performance analytics in handball.

entry.title: Researchers find planner's objective, not predictor accuracy, limits long-horizon performance in latent world models on TwoRoom task [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A study reproducing LeWorldModel on the TwoRoom environment shows that failures in long-horizon planning stem from the planner's objective function rather than the predictor's accuracy. The predictor's imagined states remain relatively accurate far beyond the planner's horizon, but the cross-entropy-method planning objective saturates and can even decrease cost when moving away from the goal, limiting effective planning. The researchers demonstrate that replacing only the planner's objective, without retraining or additional computation, dramatically improves goal-reaching success at long horizons from 26.0% to 98.0%, matching short-horizon performance and reducing computational budget. They also find that a learned planning head prioritizes reachability over spatial proximity, indicating that the model encodes information the planner cannot effectively use under the current objective.

entry.title: Researchers audit test-time budget allocation in neural combinatorial optimization, finding no detectable gain in uniform workloads but significant improvement under distribution shift [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers evaluated whether non-uniform allocation of a fixed sampling budget improves neural combinatorial optimization (NCO) solvers' performance. They found that for in-distribution workloads, such as uniform TSP-100 instances, the apparent gains from allocation were indistinguishable from zero when measured out of sample, indicating that previously reported improvements may be due to sampling luck rather than real benefit. However, under distribution shift involving mixed uniform and clustered instances, a pre-registered experiment showed that allocation guided by held-out sample statistics improved best-of-k solution quality by over 11% for two solvers (AM and SymNCO) at equal evaluation budgets, while a more robust solver (POMO) showed no significant gain. The study provides a correction procedure, reporting checklist, and releases all data and code to support reproducibility and accurate measurement of allocation gains in NCO.

entry.title: Researchers introduce TRAPSBench to show vision-language models encode but fail to express epistemic restraint, with low abstention despite internal detection of uncertainty [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers developed TRAPSBench, a video benchmark with 1,404 physics pairs designed to test vision-language models' ability to abstain when visual evidence is insufficient. They found that while models internally recognize when abstention is needed, they rarely express it, achieving a maximum Penalized Epistemic Calibration Score (PECS) of 0.292 across 16 models from five families. Linear probes decoded answerability from hidden states with up to 0.91 AUROC, indicating the bottleneck lies in expression rather than perception. The study also revealed that models detect textual uncertainty about four times more effectively than visual uncertainty, and the findings were consistent across open-weight model families including Qwen, Gemma, and LLaVA. The authors suggest that bridging the gap between internal representation and output expression will require interventions at the output stage to improve epistemic restraint in vision-language models.

entry.title: Researchers introduce MK-TGAN, a graph neural network-based generative model for synthetic transcriptomic data that integrates biological knowledge to improve realism and utility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers present a comparative analysis of generative models for synthetic transcriptomic data, focusing on incorporating prior biological knowledge through gene graphs to better capture real-world gene patterns. They introduce three variants of Generative Adversarial Networks, highlighting MK-TGAN, a multi-kernel model leveraging graph neural networks, which outperforms others in producing biologically plausible and realistic synthetic data. The study addresses challenges in biomedical data such as imbalances, biases, and ethical constraints by using synthetic data generation to enhance dataset quality and utility. Results demonstrate that integrating prior knowledge improves model performance, with MK-TGAN consistently generating superior synthetic transcriptomic samples suitable for downstream biomedical research tasks.

entry.title: Researchers introduce ORBIT training paradigm for time series foundation models, improving control over pre-training distributions and zero-shot forecasting performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers present ORBIT (Omni-Range Bootstrap Incremental Training), a new training approach for time series foundation models that explicitly controls pre-training distributions across domain imbalance, context lengths, prediction horizons, and missing data. They apply ORBIT to train Falcon-2.0, a univariate encoder-only Transformer with missingness-aware tokenization and parallel patch prediction, and introduce Rank-Guided Cross-Depth Alignment to enhance training efficiency without extra inference cost. Evaluations on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench benchmarks show that models trained with ORBIT achieve strong zero-shot forecasting performance across diverse domains and frequencies, demonstrating the effectiveness of this training regime for large-scale heterogeneous time series data.

entry.title: Researchers introduce SciFigBench to evaluate vision-language models on scientific figures, revealing differences in behavioral reliability under uncertainty [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed SciFigBench, a diagnostic benchmark designed to assess vision-language models (VLMs) on scientific figure understanding, focusing on perception, reasoning, and behavioral reliability when visual evidence is missing or misleading. The benchmark includes 250 figures with extensive human annotations and over 34,000 evaluation setups involving image transformations and probes to stress test models' responses under uncertainty. The study proposes the Admittance-Resistance-Inductance (A-R-I) framework to measure whether models acknowledge insufficient evidence, resist misleading context, and infer cautiously from partial information. Results show that while GPT-5.2 achieves high description quality and reasoning accuracy, it hallucinates unreadable content in most cases. In contrast, Gemini 3.1 Pro admits uncertainty more frequently and demonstrates stronger resistance to misleading inputs, highlighting that high accuracy alone does not ensure behavioral reliability critical for scientific applications.

entry.title: Researchers propose black-box adversarial attack tasks as large-scale benchmarks for global optimization methods in high-dimensional spaces [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers argue that existing global optimization benchmarks are limited by their small size and reliance on outdated analytical functions, which may bias method development. They propose using black-box adversarial attack tasks as valuable benchmarks for testing global optimization methods in many-dimensional spaces. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of various evolutionary algorithms and metaheuristics in solving example black-box adversarial attack problems, aiming to align global optimization research with modern machine learning challenges.

entry.title: Researchers model pricing and default token allocation in large language model reasoning services as a Stackelberg game, deriving optimal user customization and provider defaults [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers study a large language model (LLM) service where providers set per-token prices and default reasoning-token allocations, while users can accept, customize, or exit. They model this interaction as a Stackelberg game, deriving the user's unique optimal allocation and characterizing provider defaults through a three-regime rule, proving equilibrium existence. Experiments on reasoning models across math and science benchmarks validate the accuracy-token tradeoff and show how model and task features influence equilibrium prices and allocations.

entry.title: Researchers develop Faraday, a 27B-parameter AI Scientist that surpasses Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 in replicating scientific papers using a rubric-based evaluation system [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have created Faraday, a 27-billion-parameter AI agent designed to replicate scientific research papers, outperforming Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 on held-out replication tasks. The team developed Replica, a scalable task space for paper replication, and introduced an automated rubric-based judge that aligns closely with human assessments to provide reward signals during training. Faraday leverages coding agents as tools and demonstrates a more scientifically principled approach in qualitative analyses. This work aims to advance AI agents capable of long-horizon scientific innovation without requiring complex experimental setups, potentially supporting more reliable and scalable scientific replication in the future.

entry.title: Researchers introduce UltraIR, a 100M-parameter foundation model for infrared spectroscopy enabling simulation-to-real transfer learning across diverse chemical sensing tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed UltraIR, a foundation model with over 100 million parameters designed for infrared (IR) spectroscopy that enables simulation-to-real transfer learning for chemical sensing and analysis from molecules to complex samples. UltraIR is pretrained on about 60 million simulated IR spectra and fine-tuned for various downstream tasks, outperforming conventional machine-learning and task-specific deep-learning methods. It demonstrates strong performance even with limited labeled experimental data and supports zero-shot inference across different spectrometers and laboratories, offering a scalable and adaptable approach to chemical sensing in real-world applications.

entry.title: Researchers propose Reduced Matrix Multiplication, an input-adaptive method to cut Transformer inference costs by selecting matrix slices without retraining, showing efficiency gains on models from 1B to 70B parameters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers introduce Reduced Matrix Multiplication (RMM), a training-free, input-adaptive technique that reduces the computational cost of Transformer-based language model inference by selecting informative slices along matrix contraction dimensions without altering model weights. RMM offers a controllable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency and demonstrates robustness across various model sizes, tasks, and settings, including multimodal vision-language inference. Benchmarks on NVIDIA A100 hardware indicate that RMM's computational savings translate into practical runtime improvements, especially for longer input sequences, highlighting its potential as a scalable approach for optimizing inference in large language models.

entry.title: Researchers propose ARMDIL, an MLLM-based ensemble routing system for cross-dataset image classification that dynamically selects vision backbones to improve adaptability and interpretability [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers introduce ARMDIL, an Adaptive Router for Multi-Domain Image classification using multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to dynamically route images to the most suitable vision backbone among convolutional neural networks, self-supervised learners, and vision-language models. This ensemble is trained on a unified label space from multiple diverse image datasets to address challenges in generalizing across domains and difficulty levels. Empirical evaluations reveal the distinct strengths and weaknesses of each architecture across different visual domains, with ARMDIL performing competitively against specialized training-based routers. The system enhances adaptability by allowing new information integration through prompt modifications and improves interpretability via natural language reasoning traces, advancing the development of more reliable general-purpose vision systems such as AI assistants and autonomous robots.

entry.title: Researchers analyze concept drift detection methods for malware classification models, comparing One-Class SVM, Minibatch K-Means, and Maximum Mean Discrepancy approaches [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers studied the impact of concept drift-changes in data properties over time-on machine learning models used for malware detection, which can degrade as attackers modify malware. They evaluated three automated drift detection techniques: a novel One-Class Support Vector Machine (OCSVM) method, Minibatch K-Means (MK-Means), and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), across four classifiers including Multilayer Perceptron and Random Forest. The study compared three retraining scenarios: static (no retraining), periodic (constant retraining), and drift-aware (retraining only upon drift detection). Results showed that all three detection methods maintained classification accuracy comparable to periodic retraining but with greater efficiency by reducing unnecessary retraining. The OCSVM-based drift-aware retraining generally outperformed the other approaches, supporting its effectiveness for adaptive malware classification.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Synthetic Persona Pretraining to align AI assistant values from the start of pretraining, improving adherence and robustness in models up to 3B parameters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers propose Synthetic Persona Pretraining (SPP), a method that integrates desired assistant personas from the beginning of AI model pretraining by annotating documents with value-aligned reflections and binding the persona through post-training dialogue data. This approach contrasts with traditional alignment methods applied after pretraining, which can result in superficial value integration and misalignment. By training models up to 3 billion parameters on 500 billion tokens, SPP demonstrated improved constitution adherence, jailbreak resistance, and reduced misalignment in moral dilemmas without sacrificing capabilities. The study highlights that early intervention in pretraining is crucial, as introducing SPP only at the end yields weaker value adherence and less aligned decision-making. The effectiveness of SPP depends on persona binding and scales with the pretraining budget, suggesting that embedding values from token zero is a more effective strategy for aligning autonomous language models with human values.

entry.title: Researchers introduce unmasking growth complexity to optimize masking diffusion schedules for discrete sampling with certified KL error bounds [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers study masking diffusion for discrete sampling and propose a path-resolved measure of data geometry called unmasking growth complexity (UGC), which controls Kullback--Leibler (KL) discretization error and unifies analysis of Bernoulli-subset and fixed-cardinality unmasking schemes. They develop optimized single-block and multi-block schedules in log-reveal-odds coordinates and show how UGC increments can be estimated from samples, enabling certified-optimal samplers that achieve prescribed KL error with high probability and iteration complexity close to an oracle procedure. The aggregate UGC mass connects to classical multivariate dependence and complexity measures from prior discrete diffusion analyses. In the fine-partition limit, the squared integral of the square-root UGC density determines the leading-order optimal Euler discretization error. Examples demonstrate significant dimension-dependent improvements over coarse schedules, including roughly square-root dimension gains achievable with a constant number of adaptively placed blocks.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Vero benchmark to evaluate AI agents' ability to jointly synthesize implementations and formal proofs across multi-module software repositories [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Vero, the first benchmark designed to assess AI agents' capacity to generate both implementations and machine-checked proofs for multi-module software repositories. Vero includes 43 real-world instances spanning languages like Python, Dafny, Verus, and Coq, covering domains from cryptographic protocols to distributed systems, and supports evaluation of both proof-only and combined code-and-proof synthesis. The benchmark features a multi-module Lean 4 repository format with curated formal specifications and reference implementations, along with an audit mechanism allowing agents to identify specification unsatisfiability or reference code errors. Evaluations of leading AI coding agents with Lean toolchain access showed the strongest agent fully solved only 27 of 43 instances and failed to close specifications on the most challenging repositories, highlighting current limitations in repository-scale verified software synthesis. The Vero benchmark, curation pipeline, and evaluation tools have been publicly released to facilitate further research in trustworthy AI-generated software.

entry.title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2608.13545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern language models are trained on heterogeneous web-scale text corpora. Consequently, studying knowledge and skill acquisition is difficult, as prior exposure to related content is hard to characterize. To address this challenge, we introduce LITTLECURRICULUM, a curated 88B-token pretraining corpus tailored to U.S. elementary school material, explicitly excluding concepts, facts, and vocabulary taught above Grade 5. Training a 5B-parameter LLM from scratch on LITTLECURRICULUM yields LITTLELEARNER, a model with sufficient language competence for open-ended evaluation, yet with clear knowledge and capability boundaries mapped to interpretable curriculum guidelines. We release LITTLECURRICULUM and LITTLELEARNER as a developmentally restricted sandbox to study how models acquire, represent, and use data under a well-defined training scope. We illustrate the sandbox's utility in a first suite of experiments on injecting new knowledge through post-training and in-context learning. These methods let LITTLELEARNER better utilize existing knowledge, but do not raise out-of-scope capabilities. Our findings underscore the value of this controlled environment for future investigations.

entry.title: MatchMiner-AI: Open-source, Privacy-preserving Cancer Clinical Trial Matching using Artificial Intelligence [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2412.17228v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Background: Clinical trials are essential to advancing cancer treatments, but fewer than 10% of adults with cancer enroll in therapeutic trials. Open-source AI trial matching tools could democratize access to trial options. Methods: We created MatchMiner-AI, co-developed with practicing clinical oncologists and trained on synthetic electronic health record (EHR) data. It uses open-weight LLMs to summarize patient histories from unstructured EHR text and extract target populations from trial eligibility documents. Embedding and re-ranking models were distilled to retrieve and rank trial and patient suggestions. Multifaceted evaluation was performed, including retrospective quantification of distillation fidelity; applying a closed-source LLM as judge of patient summarization and matching; and evaluation of candidate matches by oncologists. Results: Across retrospective evaluations of distillation fidelity, the pipeline outperformed a baseline text-embedding model, improving mean average precision (MAP) at 20 from 0.44 (95% CI 0.44-0.45) to 0.95 (95% CI 0.95-0.96) for trial-enrolled patients and from 0.38 (95% CI 0.37-0.38) to 0.94 (95% CI 0.93-0.94) for patients who received standard of care therapies. In a 50-patient sample selected for comparison between MatchMiner-AI and a rules-based tumor genomic trial matching algorithm, MatchMiner-AI retrieved trials for all patients, as opposed to 19 patients (38%) who had tumor genomic data available. Among those 19 patients, 80% of 256 trial suggestions retrieved by MatchMiner-AI were deemed reasonable considerations by a frontier LLM, vs 53% of 113 suggestions retrieved by the rules-based approach. Conclusion: MatchMiner-AI is an open-source, open-weights, clinical trial matching AI pipeline for oncology. Synthetic training data, model weights, inference tools, and demonstration frontends are publicly available.

entry.title: Surrogate Substitution Preserves PHI Detectability: A Multi-Detector Equivalence Study [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2608.03172v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Structure-preserving de-identification replaces protected health information (PHI) with realistic same-type surrogates -- "Anna S." becomes "Maria S.", not [NAME] -- so that clinical text stays fluent and downstream tools keep working. But this only helps if the substitution does not itself corrupt the signal those tools rely on. We ask a narrow, testable question: on the spans a de-identifier actually masks, can downstream PHI detectors still find the surrogate? We introduce a paired, multi-detector evaluation protocol that (i) scores utility only on masked spans, decoupling coverage from utility; (ii) uses equivalence testing (TOST) rather than null-hypothesis significance testing, which is uninformative at our sample size (57k paired spans); and (iii) builds a surrogate-failure typology separating fixable generator defects from intrinsic detector limits. Across 11 detectors, 7 benchmarks, and 7 languages (1,750 documents), recall on masked spans moves from 76.1% to 74.9% -- a change our equivalence test shows is statistically equivalent to zero within a +/-2-point margin (p ~ 3e-9), with detector ranking preserved. The residual loss does not reflect detectors getting worse at PHI: it concentrates in malformed and out-of-distribution surrogates (truncation Chicago -> Illino, salience loss Cedars-Sinai -> Vidant). A redaction floor and an open-source surrogate baseline indicate the effect is a property of well-formed substitution, not of one tool. We release the evaluation subsets, scoring code, and an interactive dashboard at https://custodianai.pages.dev so the protocol can audit any structure-preserving transform.

entry.title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments: Results from a 41-day live challenge on the aggregated German transmission-grid load [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2608.05018v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Short-term load forecasting (STLF) plays a vital role in the electric power industry. It is relevant for critical infrastructure. STLF is no longer purely a performance and accuracy problem, because determinism, fail-safe handling, minimal-attack surface, and no dead code are software-engineering requirements rather than optional extras. This report describes results from a 41-day live challenge that evaluated an STLF pipeline for the aggregated German transmission-grid load. The STLF pipeline predicts the 24 hourly load values of a target day from European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity (ENTSO-E) data. It is based on the open-source Python library spotforecast2-safe, which tries to implement the EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments by design. The STLF pipeline includes gap- and anomaly-aware data preprocessing, calendar and weather covariates, and a forecasting algorithm. Forecast quality is compared to the official ENTSO-E day-ahead forecast. The spotforecast2-safe pipeline beats the ENTSO-E baseline. In-context models show competitive performance. Transparent, deterministic, low-cost, and auditable local models (referred to as macl2l in this report) are competitive with more than 100-million-parameter large, energy-intensive pre-trained foundation models such as chronos-2. The challenge implementation, the submission history of all teams, and the archived leaderboard are publicly available.

entry.title: Recursive Synthesis for Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2608.05466v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-quality long-horizon training data for terminal agents is expensive to produce, often costing hundreds to thousands of dollars per task, because each task must keep the instruction, environment, reference solution, and verifier mutually consistent. Human authoring does not scale, and direct generation with large language models (LLMs) often breaks these dependencies. We present Recursive Synthetic Terminal Tasks (RST), a recursive verified synthesis framework for constructing long-horizon terminal-agent tasks at scale. Starting from verified seed tasks, RST extends the reference solution, realigns the verifier and instruction to the new workflow, validates the result in a fresh sandbox, and reuses accepted tasks as seeds for subsequent rounds. Across fifteen recursive rounds, RST produces 37,484 synthesized terminal-agent tasks at roughly $0.05 per task. Task difficulty increases substantially over rounds: the median reference solution grows from 67 to 374 lines, the median number of executed commands grows from 40 to 244, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro pass@4 drops from 90% at R1 to 2.5% at R15. To demonstrate training utility, we collect rejection-sampled Qwen3.5 trajectories on the synthesized tasks and use them for supervised fine-tuning. Fine-tuning on these trajectories improves Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B by up to 10 points on Terminal-Bench 2, Terminal-Bench Hard, and Long-Horizon Terminal Bench, while agentic PPO lifts Qwen3.5-27B to 49.44%, 32.00%, and 22.07% on the three benchmarks, corresponding to relative gains of 20.0%, 41.2%, and 21.9% over the base model. Moreover, after 15 rounds, the recursion shows no ceiling: synthesis yield and validation rates remain stable as difficulty keeps climbing, indicating that the process can continue well beyond the scale reported here.

entry.title: Rule of Thumb: Explaining Artificial Intelligence Systems using Partial Information [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2608.10766v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) seeks to explain how an Artificial Intelligence (AI) system arrived at a particular decision. We propose ''Rule of Thumb'' (RoT) explanations, a new approach to XAI based upon a novel formulation that identifies the most relevant features for predicting the behaviour of an AI system, for a particular datapoint. We show how RoT is well-suited to enable XAI in: (a) zero-shot classification using large language models (LLMs), (b) auditing of opaque AI systems without model access, and (c) the use of AI in scientific discovery. Additionally, RoT meets specific requirements from leading AI regulations, provides a familiar interface and visualisations for XAI practitioners, is model-agnostic, and is substantially faster than alternatives. Code available at: https://github.com/KaiRawal/Rule-of-Thumb-Explaining-Artificial-Intelligence-Systems-using-Partial-Information

entry.title: OEIS Open: How many conjectures can language models turn into theorems? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2608.11941v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct OEIS Open, a benchmark based on 492 open mathematical conjectures from the OEIS, formalized in Lean by Tsoukalas et al. Whereas these conjectures had previously been attempted only with a bespoke agent, our open-source evaluation code runs any generic language model (LM) against them, and is secure against LM cheating attempts. We find that LMs equipped with a minimal set of tools resolve 147 of these conjectures with a budget of \$50 per attempt, scoring 30% on OEIS Open. OEIS Open Lite is a random subset of 100 conjectures for cheaper evaluation. When evaluated with a budget of \$200 per attempt, the best current LM scores 44% on OEIS Open Lite. Giving LMs access to the mathematics literature via 476,000 papers from arXiv did not increase performance on OEIS Open Lite, and nor did using more sophisticated agent loops. The conjectures covered in this work are of uncertain mathematical significance, and most have likely received little previous attention. Nevertheless, our results show that LMs can resolve open research conjectures autonomously and at modest cost.

entry.title: Enhancing In-Hospital Mortality Prediction Using Multi-Representational Learning with LLM-Generated Expert Summaries [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2411.16818v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To evaluate a multi-representational framework in which large language model (LLM)-generated expert summaries of intensive care unit (ICU) notes are fused with physiology for in-hospital mortality (IHM) prediction, and to determine how much of the resulting gain is non-redundant with the notes themselves. Using MIMIC-III (19,211 first ICU stays, 12.83% mortality), we encoded 48-hour physiology, clinical notes, and LLM summaries generated under a prompt forbidding prognostication, then fused them. Redundancy was assessed by ridge recoverability, linear probes, and retrained ablations substituting a note-orthogonal residual or a patient-shuffled summary embedding. On 3,843 held-out stays, fusion reached AUPRC 0.4977/AUROC 0.8429 versus 0.3625/0.7770 for physiology alone. Ridge regression from note embeddings explained 40.8% of summary-embedding variance. The note-orthogonal residual retained a minority of the gain (+0.0258 AUPRC, 95% CI 0.005--0.047; 28%), while patient-shuffled summaries fell below the reference. Summaries improve prediction patient-specifically, but predominantly by reorganizing information the notes already contain.

entry.title: Cueless EEG imagined speech for subject identification: dataset and benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2501.09700v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals have emerged as a promising modality for biometric identification. While previous studies have explored the use of imagined speech with semantically meaningful words for subject identification, most have relied on additional visual or auditory cues. In this study, we introduce a cueless EEG-based imagined speech paradigm, where subjects imagine the pronunciation of semantically meaningful words without any external cues. This innovative approach addresses the limitations of prior methods by requiring subjects to select and imagine words from a predefined list naturally. The dataset comprises over 4,350 trials from 11 subjects across five sessions. We assess a variety of classification methods, including traditional machine learning techniques such as Support Vector Machines (SVM) and XGBoost, as well as time-series foundation models and deep learning architectures specifically designed for EEG classification, such as EEG Conformer and Shallow ConvNet. A session-based hold-out validation strategy was employed to ensure reliable evaluation and prevent data leakage. Our results demonstrate outstanding classification accuracy, reaching 97.93%. These findings highlight the potential of cueless EEG paradigms for secure and reliable subject identification in real-world applications, such as brain-computer interfaces (BCIs).

entry.title: Yes, Q-learning Helps Offline In-Context RL [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2502.17666v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing offline in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) methods have predominantly relied on supervised training objectives, which are known to have limitations in offline RL settings. In this study, we explore the integration of RL objectives within an offline ICRL framework. Through experiments on more than 150 GridWorld and MuJoCo environment-derived datasets, we demonstrate that optimizing RL objectives directly improves performance by approximately 30% on average compared to widely adopted Algorithm Distillation (AD), across various dataset coverages, structures, expertise levels, and environmental complexities. Furthermore, in the challenging XLand-MiniGrid environment, RL objectives doubled the performance of AD. Our results also reveal that the addition of conservatism during value learning brings additional improvements in almost all settings tested. Our findings emphasize the importance of aligning ICRL learning objectives with the RL reward-maximization goal, and demonstrate that offline RL is a promising direction for advancing ICRL.

entry.title: Exploring Sparsity for Parameter Efficient Fine Tuning Using Wavelets for Vision [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2505.12532v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Efficiently adapting large pretrained models is critical under tight compute and memory budgets. While Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods like LoRA achieve efficiency through low-rank updates, their discrete rank constraint limits fine-grained parameter control and confines adaptations to low-dimensional subspaces. We propose Wavelet Fine-Tuning (WaveFT), which learns sparse updates in the wavelet domain of weight matrices, enabling fine-grained control over trainable parameters well below LoRA's minimum rank. Wavelet bases provide semi-local receptive fields that aggregate spatially coherent gradients, offering better coverage than direct weight sparsity (SHiRA) without the destructive interference of global Fourier bases (FourierFT). We provide theoretical analysis showing: (i) sparse methods achieve high-rank updates, avoiding LoRA's subspace bottleneck and enabling higher representational capacity, and (ii) a gradient coverage framework explaining when WaveFT is preferable. We perform experiments across text-to-image generation, image classification, and language understanding. WaveFT demonstrates state-of-the-art results among PEFT methods for vision tasks, where wavelets effectively capture sparse gradient structure through improved coverage, while performing comparably on NLP tasks. WaveFT has officially been included in the Hugging Face PEFT library (huggingface.co/docs/peft/en/package_reference/waveft).

entry.title: Unlearning at Scale: State-Exact Trace-Preserving Deletion in Billion-Parameter Language Models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2508.12220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can a prospectively instrumented training continuation reproduce a deletion counterfactual exactly after selected examples leave its replay dataset? We study a trace-preserving counterfactual that fixes recorded execution controls while assigning requested identifiers zero contribution. The guarantee is prospective: the original run must record this execution provenance and retain an eligible uncontaminated checkpoint. Under pinned single-GPU environments, replay from a token store materialized without the requested rows reconstructs a separately executed trace oracle bit-for-bit in model and optimizer state. Pythia 160M is exact across four deletion geometries; Pythia 2.8B matches all 2,775,208,960 model-state elements for a random 5% request; and Llama 3.2 1B is exact after omitting 400 of 4,000 TOFU examples from replay storage. These results establish billion-parameter state exactness. They do not establish cheap deletion, because dispersed requests can force nearly full replay. We release standardized TOFU/OpenUnlearning measurements as descriptive diagnostics only because the frozen campaign lacks the matched controls required for a causal behavioral claim.

entry.title: DiffGRM: Diffusion-based Generative Recommendation Model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2510.21805v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) is an emerging paradigm that represents each item via a tokenizer as an n-digit semantic ID (SID) and predicts the next item by autoregressively generating its SID conditioned on the user's history. However, two structural properties of SIDs make ARMs ill-suited. First, intra-item consistency: the n digits jointly specify one item, yet the left-to-right causality trains each digit only under its prefix and blocks bidirectional cross-digit evidence, collapsing supervision to a single causal path. Second, inter-digit heterogeneity: digits differ in semantic granularity and predictability, while the uniform next-token objective assigns equal weight to all digits, overtraining easy digits and undertraining hard digits. To address these two issues, we propose DiffGRM, a diffusion-based GR model that replaces the autoregressive decoder with a masked discrete diffusion model (MDM), thereby enabling bidirectional context and any-order parallel generation of SID digits for recommendation. Specifically, we tailor DiffGRM in three aspects: (1) tokenization with Parallel Semantic Encoding (PSE) to decouple digits and balance per-digit information; (2) training with On-policy Coherent Noising (OCN) that prioritizes uncertain digits via coherent masking to concentrate supervision on high-value signals; and (3) inference with Confidence-guided Parallel Denoising (CPD) that fills higher-confidence digits first and generates diverse Top-K candidates. Experiments show consistent gains over strong generative and discriminative recommendation baselines on multiple datasets, improving NDCG@10 by 6.9%-15.5%. Code is available at https://github.com/liuzhao09/DiffGRM.

entry.title: Automated Design Optimization via Strategic Search with Large Language Models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2511.22651v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optimization methods have long advanced many fields, yet they struggle when faced with design problems where the search space and design parameters are difficult to define. Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising alternative by dynamically interpreting design spaces and leveraging encoded domain knowledge. To this end, we present AUTO: an iterative optimization framework that treats design optimization as a strategic search guided by LLM reasoning. The framework separates high-level planning by a Strategist agent from low-level implementation by concurrent Implementor agents, iteratively refining designs through explore-exploit strategies. We demonstrate AUTO on three GPU code optimization problems. For chemical kinetics, AUTO outperforms in-lab-optimized code by up to 1.74$\times$ for problem sizes up to $10^5$ cells. For matrix multiplication, AUTO achieves up to 94\% of cuBLAS double-precision performance. For KernelBench, we achieve speedups of up to 118$\times$ over PyTorch baselines across 29 problems spanning individual operators and full neural network architectures; however, cheating was frequently observed. A posteriori analysis reveals 50~--~70\% alignment with Bayesian optimization sampling strategies. All AUTO simulations ran within 100 iterations (about 10 hours), with estimated costs of \$15~--~159 per run for proprietary models. Furthermore, AUTO is built entirely on open-source LLMs and libraries, demonstrating affordability and data privacy. Given AUTO's generizability and flexibility, future work will explore domains beyond GPUs and supercomputing.

entry.title: Security and Detectability Analysis of Unicode Text Watermarking Methods against Large Language Models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2512.13325v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Securing digital text is becoming increasingly relevant due to the widespread use of large language models. Individuals' fear of losing control over data when it is being used to train such machine learning models or when distinguishing model-generated output from text written by humans. Digital watermarking provides additional protection by embedding an invisible watermark within the data that requires protection. However, little work has been taken to analyze and verify if existing digital text watermarking methods are secure and undetectable by large language models. In this paper, we investigate the security-related area of watermarking and machine learning models for text data. In a controlled testbed of three experiments, ten existing Unicode text watermarking methods were implemented and analyzed across six large language models: GPT-5, GPT-4o, Teuken 7B, Llama 3.3, Claude Sonnet 4, and Gemini 2.5 Pro. The findings of our experiments indicate that, especially the latest reasoning models, can detect a watermarked text. Nevertheless, all models fail to extract the watermark unless implementation details in the form of source code are provided. We discuss the implications for security researchers and practitioners and outline future research opportunities to address security concerns.

entry.title: RadarGen: Automotive Radar Point Cloud Generation from Cameras [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2512.17897v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present RadarGen, a diffusion model for synthesizing realistic automotive radar point clouds from multi-view camera imagery. RadarGen adapts efficient image-latent diffusion to the radar domain by representing radar measurements in bird's-eye-view form that encodes spatial structure together with radar cross section (RCS) and Doppler attributes. A lightweight recovery step reconstructs point clouds from the generated maps. To better align generation with the visual scene, RadarGen incorporates BEV-aligned depth, semantic, and motion cues extracted from pretrained foundation models, which guide the stochastic generation process toward physically plausible radar patterns. Conditioning on images makes the approach broadly compatible, in principle, with existing visual datasets and simulation frameworks, offering a scalable direction for multimodal generative simulation. Evaluations on large-scale driving data show that RadarGen captures characteristic radar measurement distributions and reduces the gap to perception models trained on real data, marking a step toward unified generative simulation across sensing modalities.

entry.title: Architecture Before the Formula: Individuating Neural Architecture Beyond the Composite Map [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2601.11618v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neural architecture is often identified by module syntax, computation graphs, or the composite functions they realize. These descriptions answer different identity questions. We study the represented process available at a receiver: an actual factorization $B_j=G_jQ_j$ in which $Q_j(x)$ is the intermediate state supplied for further computation. Forgetting the presentation and retaining only $\ker Q_j$ yields the predecessor distinctions preserved at that cut. For a fixed branch, this extensional shadow exactly classifies unmarked surjective factorizations up to unique carrier re-presentation, but it does not determine marked receiver organization or the accessibility of retained information to restricted continuations. Under composition the relevant interface is $Q_{j,\theta}A$, so downstream architectural distinctions depend on the states produced upstream. An exact two-token construction shows that local and attention schemas are distinction-equivalent after one injective prefix and inequivalent after another, even though neither prefix loses predecessor information. The result exposes a context dependence hidden by modular architecture labels and motivates architecture comparison at the represented-process level.

entry.title: Safe Exploration via Policy Priors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2601.19612v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Safe exploration is a key requirement for reinforcement learning (RL) agents to learn and adapt online, beyond controlled (e.g. simulated) environments. In this work, we tackle this challenge by utilizing suboptimal yet conservative policies (e.g., obtained from offline data or simulators) as priors. Our approach, SOOPER, uses probabilistic dynamics models to optimistically explore, yet pessimistically fall back to the conservative policy prior if needed. We prove that SOOPER guarantees safety throughout learning, and establish convergence to an optimal policy by bounding its cumulative regret. Extensive experiments on key safe RL benchmarks and real-world hardware demonstrate that SOOPER is scalable, outperforms the state-of-the-art and validate our theoretical guarantees in practice.

entry.title: Doctorina MedBench: A Dialogue-Based Benchmark and Evaluation Framework for Agent-Based Medical AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: arXiv:2603.25821v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present Doctorina MedBench, an evaluation framework for agent-based medical AI based on the simulation of physician-patient interactions.
